proposal.distinction: Retain local exception attachment: Type 9 exclusion affects regulated_services; ordinary-course guidance affects services_as_business; expense reimbursement qualifies only the no-income description within that guidance. The rival hypothesis of a separate blanket family-office exemption fails because the text anchors these qualifications to particular classifications and preserves ordinary-course modality. It could wrongly negate a trigger involving another regulated activity or exceptional business circumstances. The unresolved negation in the business/profit phrase may materially alter business classification, but does not justify inventing a second trigger formula. Both absence-of-business-and-profit and a narrower reach of negation remain grammatical questions, not approved Boolean alternatives. The supplied diagnostics contain no fact-bound counterexample with which to distinguish them.

proposal.distinction: The express conjunction supports one formal reading of the selected trigger. The strongest uncertainty lies upstream in business classification: the ordinary-course sentence can be understood as coordinating absence of business operation and absence of a profit objective, or as making non-business operation an independent alternative because of 'or'. A genuine office receiving only expense reimbursements but pursuing profit exposes that difference: the first understanding withholds the ordinary-course expectation, while the second may support it. Neither wording establishes an automatic exemption or a definitive trigger outcome, so a rival Boolean formula would overstate the source.
